title: The Forks National Historic Site

extraction.reason: Not recorded when the page was cached, and not recovered since. What the .txt shows is a tag-stripping of the .html rather than a browser rendering: it keeps the site navigation chrome, decodes entities, holds each paragraph on one line, and carries artefacts only a regex stripper leaves - a bare `--->` where a comment opened with a `>` inside it, and a fragment of a meta attribute ending `">`. Two candidates were run on 2026-09-09 and NEITHER reproduces extractedTextSha256: a regex stripper (tags to newlines, entities decoded, blank lines dropped) and Chromium's document.body.innerText through Playwright. This is not cosmetic: content/levels/winnipeg.json cites this digest as the sourceHash of its territory statement, so a shipped claim is pinned to bytes that only a machine already holding the file can produce. Someone who fetched the page and matched its sha256 still cannot check the quote.

knownStaleness.topic: A territorial statement written by Parks Canada, not by any of the nations it names
knownStaleness.problem: The sentence this level's territory statement is drawn from - `The Forks National Historic Site is on Treaty No. 1 territory: the traditional territory of the Anishinaabeg, Nehiyawak, Ininiwak, Anisininewuk, Dakota Oyate, Denesuline, and the homeland of the Red River Metis.` - is the federal site operator's wording. It is a citable statement of fact and it is NOT a nation speaking for itself. docs/content-review.md 3.2 asks for the nation's own published material for the NAMES, and level.schema.json gives a level exactly ONE nationSource field, which cannot carry seven nations. content/levels/winnipeg.json therefore names Treaty One Nation as its nationSource, which covers the seven First Nations who signed Treaty No. 1 and does not cover Nehiyawak, Ininiwak, Anisininewuk, Dakota Oyate, Denesuline or the Red River Metis as spelled here.
knownStaleness.action: before this statement is verified, either find each name on that nation's own material and record the gap, or narrow the statement to what one nationSource can carry. Do not widen the sentence beyond this page: everything it says about who the territory belongs to is in the one quoted sentence and nothing else on the page adds to it.

knownStaleness.topic: A live promotional page, revised without notice and carrying no date
knownStaleness.problem: This is a visitor-information landing page. Hours, fees and events on it change through the season and the territorial sentence sits in the same template as they do, so the hash will move for reasons that have nothing to do with the claim.
knownStaleness.action: when the hash stops matching, re-read the territorial sentence before assuming the claim moved; a changed opening-hours table is not a changed fact

grainNote: One web page and one heading, so both flags are at chapter grain because the page has no other grain to offer. The first flag is about who is entitled to say the sentence and the second is about how often the bytes move; they are separate because a re-fetch answers the second and can never answer the first.
